blocks.title: From rules to marks
blocks.body: Knowing a rule and applying it under pressure are different skills, and the gap between them is closed only by the review habit this chapter describes. Candidates who diagnose their recurring errors, return to the governing rule, and then produce fresh correct examples improve far faster than those who only complete drills once. Treat every wrong answer in this course as information about which single rule to revisit. That loop, error to rule to fresh production, is what turns study into a higher band.

examples.Review loop: Wrong answer → name the error type → re-read the rule → write two correct sentences of your own.
examples.Exam routine: Always reserve the final minutes to run the six editing passes in order.

blocks.text: This completes the course. Return to any chapter's exercises to practise until the correct forms feel automatic; the platform will keep scoring you and showing the reason and Bengali note for every item.

exercises.title: Exercise 1.1 · Identification and Correction
exercises.instructions: Each sentence below contains a subject-verb agreement error, except three, which are already correct. Rewrite each faulty sentence correctly, and for the correct ones write “Correct.” Do this with a pen before checking the key.

items.prompt: The list of approved candidates are posted on the noticeboard.
items.answer: The list of approved candidates is posted on the noticeboard.
accepted: The list of approved candidates is posted on the noticeboard.
items.bn_note: subject “list”, মাঝের “of candidates” বাদ দিলে বোঝা যায়।

items.prompt: Each of the students have submitted their assignment.
items.answer: Each of the students has submitted his or her assignment.
accepted: Each of the students has submitted his or her assignment.
Each of the students has submitted their assignment.
items.bn_note: each of সবসময় singular, তাই has।

items.prompt: The government are introducing a new tax next year.
items.answer: The government is introducing a new tax next year.
accepted: The government is introducing a new tax next year.
items.reason: Collective noun as one unit takes a singular verb in academic writing.

items.prompt: Neither the teacher nor the students was ready for the test.
items.answer: Neither the teacher nor the students were ready for the test.
accepted: Neither the teacher nor the students were ready for the test.
items.reason: With “neither…nor,” the verb agrees with the nearer subject, “students” (plural).

items.prompt: The number of accidents on this road have increased.
items.answer: The number of accidents on this road has increased.
accepted: The number of accidents on this road has increased.
items.bn_note: “the number of” সবসময় singular।

items.prompt: There is several reasons for this decline.
items.answer: There are several reasons for this decline.
accepted: There are several reasons for this decline.

items.prompt: A large amount of information were collected during the survey.
items.answer: A large amount of information was collected during the survey.
accepted: A large amount of information was collected during the survey.
items.reason: “Information” is uncountable and singular, so “amount … was.”
items.bn_note: information uncountable, singular।

items.prompt: Ten kilometres are a long way to walk in the heat.
items.answer: Ten kilometres is a long way to walk in the heat.
accepted: Ten kilometres is a long way to walk in the heat.
items.reason: A single distance is treated as one quantity: singular verb.

items.prompt: The committee has agreed on the final budget.
items.answer: Correct.
accepted: Correct.
Correct
The committee has agreed on the final budget.
items.reason: “Committee” as one unit takes the singular “has.”

items.prompt: The quality of the roads in rural areas are very poor.
items.answer: The quality of the roads in rural areas is very poor.
accepted: The quality of the roads in rural areas is very poor.

items.prompt: Poverty and illiteracy remains major obstacles to development.
items.answer: Poverty and illiteracy remain major obstacles to development.
accepted: Poverty and illiteracy remain major obstacles to development.
items.reason: Two subjects joined by “and” are plural.

items.prompt: Everyone in the two classes were given a certificate.
items.answer: Everyone in the two classes was given a certificate.
accepted: Everyone in the two classes was given a certificate.
items.bn_note: everyone singular, তাই was।

items.prompt: Not only the manager but also the workers is unhappy with the plan.
items.answer: Not only the manager but also the workers are unhappy with the plan.
accepted: Not only the manager but also the workers are unhappy with the plan.
items.reason: With “not only…but also,” the verb agrees with the nearer subject, “workers” (plural).

items.prompt: The data collected over ten years show a clear pattern.
items.answer: Correct.
accepted: Correct.
Correct
The data collected over ten years show a clear pattern.
items.reason: “Data” is treated as a plural or mass noun; “the data … show” is acceptable and consistent here.

items.prompt: My knowledge of these topics are limited.
items.answer: My knowledge of these topics is limited.
accepted: My knowledge of these topics is limited.
items.reason: “Knowledge” is uncountable and singular; subject is “knowledge,” not “topics.”

items.prompt: A number of students has failed to register on time.
items.answer: A number of students have failed to register on time.
accepted: A number of students have failed to register on time.
items.reason: “A number of” means “several” and takes a plural verb.

items.prompt: The population of the coastal cities have grown rapidly.
items.answer: The population of the coastal cities has grown rapidly.
accepted: The population of the coastal cities has grown rapidly.

items.prompt: Neither of the two proposals seem practical.
items.answer: Neither of the two proposals seems practical.
accepted: Neither of the two proposals seems practical.
items.bn_note: neither singular, তাই seems।

items.prompt: Statistics is a subject that many students find difficult.
items.answer: Correct.
accepted: Correct.
Correct
Statistics is a subject that many students find difficult.
items.reason: “Statistics” as the name of a subject is singular: “statistics is.”

items.prompt: The equipment in the laboratories need to be replaced.
items.answer: The equipment in the laboratories needs to be replaced.
accepted: The equipment in the laboratories needs to be replaced.
items.bn_note: equipment uncountable, singular।

exercises.title: Exercise 1.2 · IELTS Essay Editing
exercises.instructions: The paragraph below is from a Band 5.5 Task 2 essay. It contains ten subject-verb agreement errors. Find them, then rewrite the whole paragraph correctly.

items.prompt: Nowadays, the number of people who works from home have increased dramatically. There is many reasons for this change. First, technology allow employees to stay connected from anywhere. Second, each of the major companies now offer flexible arrangements. However, some managers believes that productivity fall when staff is not in the office. In my opinion, the advantages of remote work outweighs the disadvantages, and this trend are likely to continue.
items.answer: Nowadays, the number of people who work from home has increased dramatically. There are many reasons for this change. First, technology allows employees to stay connected from anywhere. Second, each of the major companies now offers flexible arrangements. However, some managers believe that productivity falls when staff are not in the office. In my opinion, the advantages of remote work outweigh the disadvantages, and this trend is likely to continue.
accepted: Nowadays, the number of people who work from home has increased dramatically. There are many reasons for this change. First, technology allows employees to stay connected from anywhere. Second, each of the major companies now offers flexible arrangements. However, some managers believe that productivity falls when staff are not in the office. In my opinion, the advantages of remote work outweigh the disadvantages, and this trend is likely to continue.
items.reason: Ten agreement errors: who works→work; have increased→has increased (the number is singular); There is→There are; technology allow→allows; each of … offer→offers; managers believes→believe; productivity fall→falls; staff is→staff are; advantages … outweighs→outweigh; this trend are→is.
items.bn_note: এই অনুচ্ছেদে দশটি ভুলই subject চিনে verb মিলানোর অভাবে হয়েছে। মূল কৌশল: subject আর verb-এর মাঝের সব শব্দ বাদ দিয়ে subject-টি বের করা, তারপর singular না plural সেই অনুযায়ী verb বসানো।

exercises.title: Exercise 2.1 · Tense Selection
exercises.instructions: Put the verb in brackets into the correct tense. Each item has one best answer determined by its time signal or meaning.

items.prompt: In 2008, the company (open) ______ its first overseas office.
items.answer: opened
accepted: opened

items.prompt: Since 2015, the government (invest) ______ heavily in renewable energy.
items.answer: has invested
accepted: has invested

items.prompt: At the moment, the number of tourists (rise) ______ rapidly.
items.answer: is rising
accepted: is rising
items.bn_note: at the moment মানে এখন চলছে।

items.prompt: Water (freeze) ______ at zero degrees Celsius.
items.answer: freezes
accepted: freezes

items.prompt: By the time the survey ended, attitudes (already / change) ______.
items.answer: had already changed
accepted: had already changed
items.reason: An action completed before another past event, past perfect.

items.prompt: I (know) ______ the answer to that question. (correct the tense if wrong)
items.answer: know
accepted: know
items.reason: “I am knowing” is wrong; know is stative and stays simple present.
items.bn_note: stative verb, continuous হয় না।

items.prompt: House prices (increase) ______ steadily for the last ten years.
items.answer: have been increasing
accepted: have been increasing
have increased
items.reason: “For the last ten years” reaches to now; present perfect continuous stresses the duration.

items.prompt: If this trend continues, the population (double) ______ by 2050.
items.answer: will double
accepted: will double
items.reason: A real future prediction, first-conditional future with “will.”

items.prompt: Last summer, the temperature (rise) ______ by three degrees.
items.answer: rose
accepted: rose
items.reason: “Last summer” is finished time, past simple.

items.prompt: Nowadays, more and more people (work) ______ from home.
items.answer: are working
accepted: are working
items.reason: “Nowadays” plus a current trend, present continuous.

items.prompt: The factory (close) ______ down in 1998 and has never reopened.
items.answer: closed
accepted: closed

items.prompt: Over the past decade, technology (transform) ______ the way we communicate.
items.answer: has transformed
accepted: has transformed
items.reason: “Over the past decade” reaches to now, present perfect.

items.prompt: He (have) ______ two brothers and one sister. (state, not action)
items.answer: has
accepted: has
items.reason: Possession is stative; “is having” would be wrong here.
items.bn_note: মালিকানা বোঝালে have, continuous নয়।

items.prompt: Between 2000 and 2010, unemployment (fall) ______ gradually.
items.answer: fell
accepted: fell
items.reason: A finished past range (2000 to 2010), past simple.

items.prompt: Currently, the government (consider) ______ three new proposals.
items.answer: is considering
accepted: is considering

items.prompt: She (understand) ______ the problem now, after the explanation. (correct the tense if wrong)
items.answer: understands
accepted: understands
items.reason: “Is understanding” is wrong; understand is stative, present simple.
items.bn_note: stative verb।

items.prompt: By 2030, most new cars (be) ______ electric, experts predict.
items.answer: will be
accepted: will be
items.reason: A future prediction for a future point, future simple.

items.prompt: The graph shows that consumption (drop) ______ sharply in 2012.
items.answer: dropped
accepted: dropped
items.reason: Tied to a finished year (2012), past simple.

items.prompt: So far this year, exports (grow) ______ by twelve per cent.
items.answer: have grown
accepted: have grown
items.reason: “So far this year” reaches to now, present perfect.

items.prompt: Governments (spend) ______ large sums on defence every year. (general truth)
items.answer: spend
accepted: spend
items.reason: A repeated general truth (“every year”), present simple.

exercises.title: Exercise 2.2 · Task 1 Trend Description
exercises.instructions: Write one paragraph describing the trend, using the past simple for finished data, the present perfect for the change up to the present, and a future form for the projection. Then compare with the model.

items.prompt: Write one accurate paragraph describing the trend for “Coffee consumption per person in Country X, 1990 to 2030 (projected).” Use the past simple for finished data, the present perfect for the change up to the present (assume “now” is 2025), and a future form for the projection. Notes: 1990 low, about 2 kg; rose steadily through the 1990s; 2000 reached 5 kg; fell slightly between 2005 and 2010; has risen again every year since 2010; 2025 stands at about 8 kg; projected to reach 10 kg by 2030.
items.answer: In 1990, coffee consumption in Country X was low, at roughly 2 kilograms per person. It then rose steadily throughout the 1990s, reaching 5 kilograms by 2000. Consumption fell slightly between 2005 and 2010, but it has risen every year since, and it now stands at about 8 kilograms per person. Looking ahead, the figure is projected to reach 10 kilograms by 2030.
accepted: In 1990, coffee consumption in Country X was low, at roughly 2 kilograms per person. It then rose steadily throughout the 1990s, reaching 5 kilograms by 2000. Consumption fell slightly between 2005 and 2010, but it has risen every year since, and it now stands at about 8 kilograms per person. Looking ahead, the figure is projected to reach 10 kilograms by 2030.
items.reason: was, rose, reaching, fell = finished past data with stated years (past simple). has risen = the change reaches the present (present perfect). now stands = the present situation in 2025 (present simple). is projected to reach = a future forecast.
items.bn_note: একই অনুচ্ছেদে তিনটি সময় তিন tense-এ: শেষ হওয়া ডেটা past simple, ২০১০ থেকে এ পর্যন্ত present perfect, আর ভবিষ্যতের পূর্বাভাস future form।

exercises.title: Exercise 3.1 · Article Insertion
exercises.instructions: The articles have been removed. Rewrite each sentence inserting a, an, or the where needed. Some blanks need the zero article (no word).

items.prompt: ___ education is ___ key to ___ economic development.
items.answer: Education is the key to economic development.
accepted: Education is the key to economic development.
items.reason: General uncountable “education” and “development” take zero article; “the key” is specific.

items.prompt: She is ___ most hard-working student in ___ class.
items.answer: She is the most hard-working student in the class.
accepted: She is the most hard-working student in the class.
items.reason: Superlative and a specific class both take “the.”

items.prompt: ___ chart shows ___ number of tourists visiting ___ museum.
items.answer: The chart shows the number of tourists visiting a museum.
accepted: The chart shows the number of tourists visiting a museum.

items.prompt: ___ internet has transformed ___ way people communicate.
items.answer: The internet has transformed the way people communicate.
accepted: The internet has transformed the way people communicate.
items.reason: “the internet” is unique; “the way” is specified by the clause after it.

items.prompt: He wants to become ___ honest lawyer after ___ university.
items.answer: He wants to become an honest lawyer after university.
accepted: He wants to become an honest lawyer after university.
items.reason: “an” before the vowel sound of “honest” (silent h); “university” as an institution takes zero article.
items.bn_note: honest-এর h উচ্চারিত হয় না, তাই an।

items.prompt: ___ pollution is ___ serious problem in ___ major cities.
items.answer: Pollution is a serious problem in major cities.
accepted: Pollution is a serious problem in major cities.
items.reason: General uncountable “pollution”; “a problem” first mention; general plural “cities.”

items.prompt: I read ___ interesting article yesterday. ___ article was about ___ climate change.
items.answer: I read an interesting article yesterday. The article was about climate change.
accepted: I read an interesting article yesterday. The article was about climate change.
items.reason: First mention “an,” second mention “the,” general “climate change.”

items.prompt: ___ government should invest more in ___ public transport.
items.answer: The government should invest more in public transport.
accepted: The government should invest more in public transport.
items.reason: “the government” is specific; “public transport” is a general uncountable.

items.prompt: ___ United States and ___ United Kingdom signed ___ agreement.
items.answer: The United States and the United Kingdom signed an agreement.
accepted: The United States and the United Kingdom signed an agreement.
items.reason: These country names take “the”; “an agreement” first mention.
items.bn_note: the United States, the United Kingdom সবসময় the নেয়।

items.prompt: ___ sun rises in ___ east.
items.answer: The sun rises in the east.
accepted: The sun rises in the east.

items.prompt: ___ poverty remains ___ obstacle to ___ progress in ___ developing world.
items.answer: Poverty remains an obstacle to progress in the developing world.
accepted: Poverty remains an obstacle to progress in the developing world.
items.reason: General “poverty” and “progress”; “an obstacle” first mention; “the developing world” is specific.

items.prompt: She gave me ___ useful advice about ___ visa process.
items.answer: She gave me useful advice about the visa process.
accepted: She gave me useful advice about the visa process.
items.reason: “advice” is uncountable (no “a”); “the visa process” is specific.
items.bn_note: advice uncountable, তাই a বসে না।

items.prompt: ___ number of ___ students who fail ___ exam is rising.
items.answer: The number of students who fail the exam is rising.
accepted: The number of students who fail the exam is rising.

items.prompt: My brother is ___ engineer, and he works for ___ large company.
items.answer: My brother is an engineer, and he works for a large company.
accepted: My brother is an engineer, and he works for a large company.

items.prompt: ___ water is essential for ___ life on ___ Earth.
items.answer: Water is essential for life on Earth.
accepted: Water is essential for life on Earth.
items.reason: General uncountables and the proper noun “Earth” take zero article.

items.prompt: We stayed in ___ hotel near ___ airport; ___ hotel was cheap.
items.answer: We stayed in a hotel near the airport; the hotel was cheap.
accepted: We stayed in a hotel near the airport; the hotel was cheap.
items.reason: First mention “a hotel,” the known “the airport,” second mention “the hotel.”

items.prompt: ___ research shows that ___ exercise improves ___ mental health.
items.answer: Research shows that exercise improves mental health.
accepted: Research shows that exercise improves mental health.
items.bn_note: research uncountable।

items.prompt: ___ environment must be protected for ___ future generations.
items.answer: The environment must be protected for future generations.
accepted: The environment must be protected for future generations.
items.reason: “the environment” is unique; “future generations” general plural.

items.prompt: He spent ___ hour reading ___ book about ___ history of ___ Bangladesh.
items.answer: He spent an hour reading a book about the history of Bangladesh.
accepted: He spent an hour reading a book about the history of Bangladesh.
items.reason: “an hour” (silent h), “a book” first mention, “the history of X” specific, proper noun “Bangladesh” zero.

items.prompt: ___ traffic in ___ capital is ___ major source of ___ air pollution.
items.answer: The traffic in the capital is a major source of air pollution.
accepted: The traffic in the capital is a major source of air pollution.
items.reason: “the traffic” specific, “the capital” specific, “a source” first mention, general “air pollution.”

items.prompt: ___ knowledge is power, but ___ information alone is not ___ knowledge.
items.answer: Knowledge is power, but information alone is not knowledge.
accepted: Knowledge is power, but information alone is not knowledge.

items.prompt: She is ___ best doctor in ___ hospital where I work.
items.answer: She is the best doctor in the hospital where I work.
accepted: She is the best doctor in the hospital where I work.

items.prompt: ___ children in ___ rural areas often lack access to ___ good schools.
items.answer: Children in rural areas often lack access to good schools.
accepted: Children in rural areas often lack access to good schools.

items.prompt: ___ economy grew by ___ five per cent in ___ first quarter.
items.answer: The economy grew by five per cent in the first quarter.
accepted: The economy grew by five per cent in the first quarter.
items.reason: “the economy” unique, “five per cent” no article, “the first quarter” ordinal.

items.prompt: ___ solar power is ___ cleaner alternative to ___ fossil fuels.
items.answer: Solar power is a cleaner alternative to fossil fuels.
accepted: Solar power is a cleaner alternative to fossil fuels.
items.reason: General uncountable “solar power,” “a cleaner alternative” first mention, general plural “fossil fuels.”

exercises.title: Exercise 3.2 · Countable versus Uncountable Error Spotting

accepted: We had a lot of homework during the holidays.

items.prompt: The company installed new softwares on every computer.

accepted: The company installed new software on every computer.

items.prompt: There were many traffics on the road this morning.

items.prompt: The hotel provides free accommodations for its staffs.
items.answer: The hotel provides free accommodation for its staff.
accepted: The hotel provides free accommodation for its staff.

items.prompt: My knowledges of physics are quite limited.

items.answer: The students carried heavy luggage to the airport.
accepted: The students carried heavy luggage to the airport.
